comparison: Perfect agreement on ChIP-seq data characterizing ZFHX3 genomic binding patterns (C3-C8, C11, C13-C15, C17-C18, C99-C100). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers noted data normalization concerns that were addressed in revisions, while OpenEval found the quantitative measurements internally consistent and well-supported by Figure 1.

Both support functional annotation analysis (C20-C23) showing ZFHX3 targets in circadian rhythm GO categories. OpenEval evaluated broader set of claims (C9-C24) including additional functional interpretations, while peer review focused on subset. Both rate as SUPPORTED and acknowledge the DAVID analysis and Figure 1 supplement data.

Disagreement on interpretation of no differential binding between timepoints (C25-C27, C105-C106). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with caveat about limited temporal resolution. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether ZFHX3 binding relates to promoter activity and suggesting additional experiments. Both acknowledge the data in Supplementary file 1 but differ on confidence in the 'poised TF' interpretation.

Both accept motif analysis data (C28-C32, C104) but express reservations about mechanistic interpretation. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while noting 'shared binding' with BMAL1:CLOCK is inference. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting additional assays beyond predictions to test the interaction hypothesis. Agreement on data quality, disagreement on strength of functional conclusions.

Strong agreement on behavioral analysis (C33-C43). Both rate SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers noted the findings were not entirely novel but consistent with previous studies and praised the adult-specific inducible deletion approach. OpenEval emphasized statistical rigor, adequate sample sizes, and consistency between DD and LD phenotypes. Both accept the wheel-running data in Figure 2.

Strong agreement on RNA-seq differential expression and ChIP-seq integration (C44-C51, C109). Both rate SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers praised the properly designed multi-omics approach and found transcriptome analysis compelling. OpenEval highlighted rigorous statistical analysis and strong association between ZFHX3+histone marks and gene expression. Both accept the mechanistic interpretation linking binding to functional consequences.

Agreement on functional enrichment of neuropeptide pathways (C52-C54, C56). Both rate SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers noted consistency with previous studies. OpenEval noted validation through multiple cited studies but flagged 'physiological impairment' claim as somewhat speculative without direct measurements. Both accept the DAVID analysis shown in Figure 3D.

Strong agreement on rhythmic transcriptome analysis using dryR (C57-C69, C110). Both rate SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers emphasized clear impact on gene expression and praised circadian phase-estimation algorithms. OpenEval detailed the systematic categorization into modules and adequate experimental design. Both accept that large fraction of rhythmic transcriptome is affected with direct and indirect effects.

Both support functional characterization of gene modules (C70-C76). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing WNT-pathway connections and enrichment of core circadian functions in phase/amplitude-changed genes. Peer reviewers (R12) accepted the module-based analysis and nuanced interpretation that clock is disrupted but not ablated. Agreement on C123 regarding Module 2 genes losing rhythmicity.

Strong agreement on core clock gene expression changes (C77-C87). Both rate SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers noted complete loss of Bmal1 rhythm and selective effects on Per genes with ~2hr phase advance. OpenEval emphasized striking Bmal1 finding and differential effects on Per vs Cry genes. Both accept the data in Figures 4A, 4B, 5C and Table 1 showing selective action on clock components.

Agreement on neuropeptide and CCG effects (C88-C96, C117-C118). Both rate SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accepted neuropeptide changes as consistent with previous studies and acknowledged severe reductions. OpenEval noted data clearly shows transcript changes but 'compromised intercellular coupling' interpretation is appropriately speculative. Both accept the data while noting functional coupling consequences are inferred.

Strong agreement on TimeTeller analysis (C97-C98). Both rate SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers praised the phase advance prediction from gene expression networks and noted it correctly predicts behavioral phenotype. OpenEval emphasized proper validation, statistical significance (p=0.0028), and consistency with behavioral data. Both strongly support this integrative molecular-behavioral analysis.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding genome topology role (C101-C104). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting CTCF co-occurrence data is solid but 3D genome organization claims are highly speculative without Hi-C or similar data. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether ZFHX3 has direct role and noting it appears to be general factor marking active chromatin. Both accept motif data but not mechanistic interpretation.

OpenEval rates C107-C108 as UNCERTAIN, noting unpublished citation cannot be verified and BMAL1 partnership claim lacks direct evidence of physical interaction. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about unpublished data and speculative BMAL1 partnership.

Agreement on mechanistic speculation (C110-C116). Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes C110 is well-supported but C111-C116 are primarily literature discussion with speculative mechanistic explanations lacking direct validation. Peer reviewers did not explicitly evaluate these scenarios but editor noted acceptance of multiple possible mechanisms. Both recognize these as hypothetical explanations for Bmal1 arrhythmicity.

Agreement on cellular distribution inference (C119-C122). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes widespread neuronal expression is inferred from differential impact on neuronal (60%) vs astrocytic (20%) genes, though this is indirect measure. Peer reviewers accepted the integrative interpretation of ZFHX3's broad presence across SCN neuronal populations. Both support the cell-type specific analysis.

Partial overlap on Module 2 genes losing rhythmicity (C123). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for C123 data but notes C124 functional consequences are speculative. Peer reviewers (R12) accepted the module characterization as part of broader rhythmic transcriptome analysis. Agreement on the data, with OpenEval more explicit about speculative nature of functional interpretation.

Agreement on adult-specific knockout rationale (C125-C132). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting global UBC-Cre deletion affects all tissues despite adult timing, limiting isolation of SCN-specific effects. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, praising inducible adult deletion as strength for isolating circadian from developmental effects. Disagreement on whether global adult knockout adequately isolates circadian function.

Strong agreement on summary conclusions (C133-C135). Both rate SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers and editors emphasized importance of genomic binding inventory and solid data on TF activity in rhythmic gene expression. OpenEval noted claims appropriately summarize comprehensive ChIP-seq and RNA-seq evidence without overstating. Both strongly support the integrative multi-omics conclusions as major contribution.

Both support background context claims (C1-C2). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting these are literature-based context statements with current study's behavioral data providing additional support. Peer reviewers accepted the broader ZFHX3 literature context as part of their evaluation of adult-specific knockout rationale. Agreement on validity of background claims.
